## Context

The second half of the isolation class (R2S1 category f): shared mutable state across concurrent writers. The exemplar is the completion-verdict cache fixed instance-by-instance in `89981d8e` — two concurrent closes derived the same `<criterion-hash>.tmp` pathname, the first `os.replace` consumed the shared temp, the second raised `FileNotFoundError`, and a best-effort `except Exception` swallowed it, so the loser silently returned 0. The class is "a process-derived or content-derived name shared across concurrent contexts"; instances keep recurring because each fix is local.

**A shared helper already exists.** `src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py::atomic_write` (118 LOC, stdlib-only leaf, ~50 call sites) already implements exactly the exemplar's fix — `mkstemp` in the target directory, write, `chmod`, `os.replace`, `unlink` on any exception. Its own module docstring names `rebar.toml` among the sites it was meant to consolidate, yet that site still hand-rolls. So this story is a **conversion of the remaining hazard sites onto the existing helper**, not the authoring of a new one, and it deliberately adds no new module. (The ticket's original guess of `src/rebar/llm/completion_cache.py` and a new `_store/unique_write.py` were both wrong: the real exemplar is `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py`.)

## Approach

**Step 1 — the audit is already done and is a deliverable.** An enumeration of cache/temp write sites in `src/rebar` classified every site as ALREADY-UNIQUE, SHARED-NAME-HAZARD, or ROOT-UNKEYED-CACHE. Result: ~30 already-unique sites (using `atomic_write`, `mkstemp`, `NamedTemporaryFile`, `mkdtemp`, or uuid4 naming), **six shared-name hazards**, and — after auditing every module-level cache and `lru_cache` — **zero root-unkeyed caches**: all are keyed by absolute path, repo root, or a stat token, and the two store-state `lru_cache`s are explicitly repo-root + overlay-signature keyed. That negative result is reported, not silently dropped.

The six hazards:

| site | derivation | atomic today |
|---|---|---|
| `review_bot/reconcile.py:177` `_write_cursor` | `p.with_suffix(".tmp")` — shared temp; swallows `OSError` | replace, shared temp |
| `_config_writer.py:279` | `target.name + ".tmp"` | replace, shared temp |
| `_cli/__init__.py:253` | `target.name + ".tmp"` | replace, shared temp |
| `_opcert_signing.py:77` | `f"{pub}.{os.getpid()}.tmp"` — pid-derived, so it collides across THREADS in the threaded MCP server | replace, shared temp |
| `_snapshot/janitor.py:300` | `f"{sha}.integrity"` written directly | **none** — torn read possible |
| `llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:507` | `self._path(id).write_text(...)` | **none** — run-scoped dir limits collision, torn-read window remains |

**Step 2 — convert.** Each site calls `fsutil.atomic_write`; sites that are deliberately best-effort keep their own `try/except` around the call, which is the contract `atomic_write`'s docstring already states. No site is left deriving its temp name solely from a content or criterion hash.

**Step 3 — regress.** One concurrency test in the shape the exemplar's own regression already established at `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verdict_cache.py:487`: a `threading.Barrier(2)` with `monkeypatch.setattr` on the module's own `os.replace`, gating only the target write, two threads, asserting both writers' effects land and no `*.tmp` residue remains. This reuses the established in-repo pattern for this exact defect class rather than inventing a harness. The store-level suites are the wrong shape here and are deliberately not used: `tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py` is a subprocess storm and `tests/interfaces/store/sync_contention_harness.py` covers sync/freshness contention, neither providing a two-writer barrier at a single file write.

For `review_bot/reconcile.py` specifically the write swallows `OSError` and returns `None`, so the assertion must be on file CONTENT, not on a return value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: a site table classifying every cache/temp write site found, with `file:line` and verdict, is committed in the change description, including the explicit negative result that no root-unkeyed cache was found.
- [ ] AC2: all six shared-name-hazard sites call `fsutil.atomic_write`, and no site derives a temp name solely from a content/criterion hash or a fixed literal. Verified by `grep -rn 'with_suffix(.*tmp\|+ \".tmp\"\|getpid()}.tmp' src/rebar` returning no write-path hits.
- [ ] AC3: a two-writer concurrency regression test passes against the converted code and fails RED against the old shared-name pattern. Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py -v`, and by the mutation check restoring a shared-temp derivation and observing the test go red.
- [ ] AC4: the two no-temp sites (`janitor.py:300`, `completion_banking.py:507`) become atomic, closing the torn-read window. Verified by the same suite asserting a reader never observes a partial file.
- [ ] AC5: no new module or helper is added — the change consumes the existing `fsutil.atomic_write`. Verified by the diff touching no new file under `src/rebar/_store/`.
- [ ] AC6: `atomic_write`'s role as the single house helper for this class is documented where the isolation helpers are documented.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py -v` — the two-writer barrier regression (AC3) and the torn-read assertions for the two previously non-atomic sites (AC4).
- `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verdict_cache.py -v` — the exemplar's existing concurrency regression still passes, proving the conversion did not regress the already-fixed site.
- `grep -rn 'with_suffix(.*tmp\|+ \".tmp\"\|getpid()}.tmp' src/rebar` — no remaining shared-name temp derivations on a write path (AC2).
- `make lint && make typecheck && make test` — the house gates, including the complexity ratchet over the touched modules.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py`, `src/rebar/_config_writer.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`, `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py` (the six hazard sites converted to `fsutil.atomic_write`)
- `tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py` (new; two-writer barrier regression + torn-read assertions)
- `docs/` (note `atomic_write` as the house helper for this class, beside the isolation helpers)
